title: The right mate of exact open localization is the inverse restriction localization factor.
statement: Let A be an arbitrary commutative ring and j:U→X an open immersion. Between the adjunction obtained by applying the ordinary open adjunction degree by degree to cochain complexes and the fixed derived open adjunction, the exact open localization comparison defines a square with the localization functors Q as horizontal sides. Its right mate is the square defined by the inverse exact localization factor for upperStar along j.

source.place: Proof step 1: the exact open adjunction unit and localization factors. Stacks 0E8I, 03DI, 03EK and 06YY.

proof.text: On a cochain representative of a homotopy-category object, the exact derived adjunction unit formula says that its unit followed by the two exact factorization maps is the localization of the ordinary cochain unit. The quotient factor isomorphisms are identities on the underlying objects, so the homotopy exact factors on the quotient object equal the cochain exact factors.

Postcompose the unit identity characterizing the mate with the upperStar factorization isomorphism. Its inverse and hom cancel, and the resulting identity is precisely the first step. Cancel that isomorphism and use injectivity of the adjunction hom equivalence to identify the mate.

theorem etaleOpenLocalizationMate
    (A : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing A]
    {U X : Scheme.{u}} (j : U ⟶ X) [IsOpenImmersion j] :
    mateEquiv
      ((openImmersionLowerShriekUpperStarAdjunction
      (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) j).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ))
      (derivedOpenImmersionLowerShriekUpperStarAdjunction (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) j)
      (TwoSquare.mk _ _ _ _
        (openImmersionLowerShriek (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) j).mapDerivedCategoryFactors.hom) =
      TwoSquare.mk _ _ _ _
        (upperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) j).mapDerivedCategoryFactors.inv
